spec_declarations.title: Inspect before proposing
spec_declarations.statement: Before a ledger mutation is proposed, the caller must obtain a ledger inspection snapshot for the resolved workspace and target context. The snapshot supplies the authoritative source revision and current context needed to construct the request; remembered conversation or a derived CRAFT.md view is not a substitute.

spec_declarations.title: One request protocol
spec_declarations.statement: Ledger mutation input uses one versioned request protocol rather than an unrelated top-level YAML contract for every ledger family. Its common envelope binds request_version, request_id, operation, target.workspace, target.context_id, target.expected_revision, and payload.

spec_declarations.title: Discriminated operation payload
spec_declarations.statement: The operation value selects exactly one operation payload shape. Payload fields are not interchangeable across gaps, blockers, decisions, definitions, or other ledger families, and a payload that does not match operation is invalid.

spec_declarations.title: First supported slice
spec_declarations.statement: The first profile supports only operation add_gap. Its payload requires gap_id, summary, severity, treatment, owner_route, status, and evidence. Any other operation returns UNSUPPORTED until its own payload semantics and mapping are defined.

spec_declarations.title: Caller and runtime ownership
spec_declarations.statement: The interpretive caller supplies operation, context_id, and the semantic payload. A trusted caller adapter may inject or copy mechanical envelope values such as request_version, request_id, the resolved workspace, and expected_revision from the inspection snapshot, but the complete assembled request is the object validated and fingerprinted by the runtime.

spec_declarations.title: Plan without mutation
spec_declarations.statement: Planning must reread the authoritative ledger, verify the workspace, context, expected revision, IDs, references, and add_gap policy, construct and validate the complete candidate, and return a stable plan or non-writing outcome. Planning grants no write authority.

spec_declarations.title: Explicit apply boundary
spec_declarations.statement: Apply accepts a validated plan identity plus required authorization, rechecks the bound source revision inside the commit boundary, and either publishes the complete candidate atomically or writes nothing. A changed source returns STALE_SOURCE; a changed plan, profile, serializer, candidate, or authorization returns PLAN_MISMATCH.

spec_declarations.title: Stable fail-closed outcome
spec_declarations.statement: Every attempt returns a ledger mutation outcome from PLAN, APPLIED, NO_OP, ALREADY_APPLIED, CONFLICT, PLAN_MISMATCH, INVALID, UNKNOWN, UNSUPPORTED, or STALE_SOURCE, with diagnostics and persistence effect sufficient for the caller to know whether ledger bytes changed.

voices.normative: A ledger inspection snapshot is the read-only, revision-bound representation of the authoritative ledger state and selected context that a caller must consume before proposing a mutation.
voices.formal: For ledger L at revision r and context c, inspect(L,c) yields S=(ledger_ref,r,c,relevant_state,constraints) without changing L; any request derived from S binds expected_revision=r.
voices.operational: Resolve the workspace, read .craft/ledger.yml, verify the requested context, calculate the source revision, and return only the current facts needed to form a supported request.
voices.plain_language: It is the fresh read the caller gets before asking to change the ledger.
voices.domain_context: In Craft ledger mutation, the snapshot prevents a model from relying only on conversation memory or CRAFT.md and gives the later request an exact expected_revision.

notation.meaning: The inspection snapshot of ledger L for context c at source revision r.

includes: Resolved workspace and authoritative ledger identity
Selected context and relevant current state
Known constraints needed by a supported operation
excludes: A derived CRAFT.md view as source of truth
conditions: It is produced by a fresh read of the authoritative ledger.

definitions.use_carefully: The snapshot is point-in-time evidence; it becomes stale when the authoritative ledger revision changes.
definitions.misuse_warning: Do not treat a snapshot as permission to write or as a replacement for the apply-time revision check.

voices.normative: A ledger mutation request is the complete versioned proposal passed to the deterministic runtime, consisting of a common envelope and exactly one payload selected by operation; it proposes meaning but does not authorize or perform a write.
voices.formal: R=(v,id,op,target(workspace,context,expected_revision),payload_op), where payload_op conforms to the schema selected by op and the normalized R is the unit fingerprinted for idempotence.
voices.operational: Assemble mechanical envelope values with the caller's semantic choice, reject unknown fields or a payload that does not match operation, and pass the complete request to planning.
voices.plain_language: It is one change request with shared addressing fields and a type-specific body.
voices.domain_context: In the first Craft slice, operation is add_gap and payload carries gap semantics; decision and blocker payloads do not exist until separately defined.

notation.meaning: A mutation request whose operation selects the matching payload contract.

includes: Protocol version and logical request identity
Resolved workspace, context ID, and expected source revision
excludes: A generic record body shared by all ledger families
conditions: The operation must be supported by the selected profile.
The payload must conform to the operation-selected contract.

definitions.use_carefully: Mechanical fields may be injected by a trusted adapter, but the full assembled request is the validated and fingerprinted object.
definitions.misuse_warning: Do not let the runtime invent missing semantic fields or reinterpret one family payload as another.
definitions.promotion_boundary: Definitions Governance or the accepted project definition owner must review promotion beyond this feature-local candidate bundle.

definitions.status_detail: Candidate feature-local meaning pending owner review.

voices.normative: An operation payload is the operation-selected semantic body of a ledger mutation request, with fields and invariants owned by exactly one supported ledger mutation operation.
voices.formal: For discriminator op, payload must belong to P_op; P_gap, P_blocker, and P_decision are distinct shapes, and payload in P_x with op not equal to x is invalid.
voices.operational: Select the payload validator from operation, validate only that family's required fields and enums, and reject unsupported operations before candidate construction.
voices.plain_language: The outside of the request stays the same; the inside changes according to the kind of ledger entry.
voices.domain_context: For v1, only P_add_gap exists and requires gap_id, summary, severity, treatment, owner_route, status, and evidence.

notation.meaning: The payload contract selected by operation op.

conditions: Exactly one supported operation owns the payload shape.

definitions.use_carefully: A shared envelope does not imply shared family semantics.
definitions.misuse_warning: Do not create a permissive values object that accepts the union of all family fields.
definitions.promotion_boundary: Definitions Governance or the accepted project definition owner must review promotion beyond this feature-local candidate bundle.

definitions.status_detail: Candidate feature-local meaning pending owner review.

voices.normative: A ledger mutation outcome is the stable, non-ambiguous response that identifies the attempted request and reports its classified result, diagnostics, bound identities, and whether authoritative ledger bytes changed.
voices.formal: O=(request_id,fingerprint,status,effect,bindings,diagnostics), with status in {PLAN,APPLIED,NO_OP,ALREADY_APPLIED,CONFLICT,PLAN_MISMATCH,INVALID,UNKNOWN,UNSUPPORTED,STALE_SOURCE} and effect explicitly write or no-write.
voices.operational: Return the same classified response shape for planning, application, replay, conflict, stale state, unsupported input, and unknown policy so the caller never infers persistence from process exit alone.
voices.plain_language: It tells the caller exactly what happened and whether the ledger changed.
voices.domain_context: Craft uses the outcome to distinguish a valid dry-run, a committed mutation, a harmless replay, and every fail-closed case.

notation.meaning: The stable classified outcome for mutation request R.

includes: Request and plan bindings where applicable
excludes: Implicit success inferred only from exit code
Silent normalization of unsupported or unknown semantics
conditions: Every attempted supported protocol request returns one classified outcome.

definitions.use_carefully: PLAN is a successful non-writing result, not evidence that apply occurred.
definitions.misuse_warning: Do not collapse UNKNOWN, UNSUPPORTED, INVALID, and CONFLICT into one generic error because their repair routes differ.

semantic_applications.rationale: The configured feature surface describes the required read but contains no canonical definition registry for this scoped concept.
The discovery proposes this boundary locally and the configured surface has no canonical registry owning it.
The family-specific part is required by the discovery but is not yet a canonical repository term in the configured surface.
The stable result vocabulary is feature-local and has no canonical registry entry in the configured surface.

layering.rationale: Definition closes the protocol meaning and first operation boundary; component placement, schemas, persistence mechanism, and delivery order remain Design work.

distill.rationale: The target is one narrow protocol slice with one supported operation and no competing definition candidates requiring comparative distillation.

identity_denominator.rationale: The feature carries explicit request and ledger IDs but does not assert or compare a closed canonical ID-to-label denominator in this Define stage.
